types.constructor: MaintenanceModeManager::new(&Arc<Container>) -> Result<Self, MaintenanceError>; captures config and weakly owns container

getDefaultDriver.defaults: missing=file; configured string retained; non-string InvalidDriver

driver.defaults: None/empty chooses default; built-ins file,array,cache; custom creator takes precedence
driver.lifecycle: one resolved driver per name per manager, concurrent calls share it; callback runs outside registry locks

extend.local: extend(name, Fn(&Container) -> Result<Arc<dyn MaintenanceMode>, MaintenanceError>) -> Result<Arc<MaintenanceModeManager>, MaintenanceError>
extend.defaults: custom factories retained by forget_drivers; existing resolved instance retained until forgotten
extend.adaptation: typed closure receives actual container; it may capture a weak manager handle or resolve the bound manager, preserving callback receiver use without PHP Closure rebinding

getDrivers.lifecycle: only resolved entries; old returned handles survive cache clearing

getContainer.errors: Unavailable after owning application is dropped

setContainer.lifecycle: retains captured configuration, creators and resolved drivers; future resolution receives selected container; weak ownership prevents cycles

forgetDrivers.lifecycle: drops resolved entries outside registry lock; no stale middleware handle; custom creators retained

activate.errors: I/O, decoding, cache, rejected writes propagate
activate.lifecycle: HTTP/Artisan/Schedule/Worker use same configured service; cache driver uses repository default TTL and current named repository

deactivate.lifecycle: same actual driver as application/commands; file removed, cache forgotten, array inactive

active.lifecycle: actual current driver status, including explicit contract replacement

data.adaptation: None represents absent/inactive data; Some(empty map) represents active empty payload. This preserves existing Rust contract and exposes the active/inactive distinction; PHP array inactive payload is []
